newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks rise to record high at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks rise to record high at open.

text.p: Toronto stocks inched further into uncharted territory at the open on Monday, boosted by bank stocks which continue to benefit from fading fears of interest rate hikes.
Traders said the market was mostly mixed and trading was quiet, with only bank stocks making a clear move early.
"It's very quiet and very mixed...it doesn't really seem there's anything to the market today," one trader said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 6.43 points to a new high of 6557.03 in thin dealings of 6.2 million shares worth C$114 million.
Advances outpaced declines 209 to 183, while 224 were flat.
Most of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes were down slightly.
Banks led the winners, gaining 30.92 points or 0.46 percent to 6730.31.

Interest-sensitive stocks have benefited from easing interest rate hike fears. Last week's softer than expected U.S. producer price index and retail sales data were seen ruling out a rate increase at the Fed's next meeting on July 1-2.

* Bombardier Corp said today it won a C$290 million Boeing contract. The airplane maker is expected to announce later this week a US$1.2 billion order from AMR Corp for 67 of its 50-seat regional jets.
